_comment: Single source of truth for the flagos platform/build matrix.
Consumed by setup.py (via json) and by CMake (via string(JSON), see
cmake/FlagosPlatforms.cmake). Editing this file is how a platform's
build switches, runtime source dir, project languages, USE_* macro,
bundled-libtorch dir and wheel local-version tag are changed.
Only genuinely platform-specific SDK path resolution (which env vars,
which default install dir) stays in the CMakeLists files; that is the
SDK-roots phase of issue #376, tracked separately.
_accelerators_comment: kernel_defaults: what the platform builds before any explicit FLAGOS_BUILD_*
environment value. Every platform starts from all-ON; the entries below are
the resolved defaults. setup.py owns this resolution at build time and CMake
applies the same values when a switch was not passed as -D.
pins: values an explicit -D/environment variable may not contradict, because
the platform cannot produce the other answer at all. The reason is shown in
the CMake FATAL_ERROR and mirrors setup.py's ValueError.
pins must equal kernel_defaults for the same switch (a pin states the only
possible value; the default already is it).
wheel_local: the wheel's PEP 440 local version segment -- the SDK it was
built against, in the same spelling the vendor's own wheels use
maca3.8.1.3). It is the build variant, not the publishing target: the
artifact goes to exactly one lane, flagos-pypi-<vendor>, so the lane is
already implied by the platform and does not belong in the filename. That
also keeps the artifact name unique across SDK variants of the same
platform, which a vendor-only segment would not (two MetaX images build two
different wheels against MACA 3.8.1.3 and 3.8.0).
tsingmicro and bpu are empty: neither publishes to a lane, so neither
artifact carries a segment and both are called plain 2.10.0. FLAGOS_WHEEL_LOCAL
overrides the value for a dev build that must pin something else.
pypi_lane: the flagos-pypi-<lane> repository this platform's wheel is
published to -- the {vendor} that build-infra's pypi_base expands to
(https://resource.flagos.net/repository/flagos-pypi-{vendor}/). This is the
publishing target and is deliberately not derived from wheel_local: that
names the build variant, and a platform publishes to one lane however many
SDK variants it builds. Empty where nothing is published (tsingmicro, bpu).
vendor_torch_libraries: whether the platform sources a vendor libtorch in
the wheel. vendor_torch_gate, when present, names the one kernel switch the
build has to compile for that to actually happen (the CUDA-ABI platforms
gate on boxing); setup.py writes the resolved value into the compatibility
manifest and CMake ignores it.

_comment: NVIDIA CUDA. FlagGems-primary by default: FLAGOS_BUILD_BOXING is off,
so the wheel does not compile the generated CUDA boxing kernels and
does not need a bundled libtorch_cuda.so -- ops route to the FlagGems
Python path and everything else reaches cpu_fallback. Boxing stays
available as an explicit opt-in (-DFLAGOS_BUILD_BOXING=ON /
FLAGOS_BUILD_BOXING=1), which is what a boxing wheel is built with.
T-Head PPU: CUDA toolchain + a bundled PPU libtorch, no native kernel
dir. FlagGems-primary by default now that FLAGOS_BUILD_BOXING is off:
the default wheel needs no PPU libtorch bundle and routes to FlagGems
(cpu_fallback for the rest). A boxing wheel is an explicit opt-in.
MetaX is a CUDA-boxing build: the generated CUDA boxing kernels
re-dispatch PrivateUse1 -> CUDA into maca's libtorch_cuda.so; the
hand-written mxcc kernels under backends/metax/ are retired. No
MACA-built liboperators exists by default, so the FlagGems C++ wrappers
stay off (an explicit FLAGGEMS_CPP=1 with FLAGGEMS_DIR still wins -- the
MACA case is a documented opt-in). FlagGems Python stays on so the
default FlagGems-primary wheel routes to the python path.
Boxing is now an explicit opt-in (-DFLAGOS_BUILD_BOXING=ON /
FLAGOS_BUILD_BOXING=1); the default wheel compiles no boxing kernels and
needs neither the MACA libtorch bundle nor a vendor torch package.
Kunlunxin XPU: a native PrivateUse1 backend. The ops live in the vendor
op library (xdnn_pytorch) and the runtime sources under kunlunxin/ call
the XPU SDK's own C runtime (libxpurt) directly, so no tensor is ever
re-dispatched onto the CUDA dispatch key and boxing stays off. The SDK
also ships a CUDA-shaped surface (cuda_runtime.h from XPU_ROOT,
libcudart.so.12 from XCUDART_ROOT) which the vendor torch uses, but the
flagos runtime does not: it is what the de-boxed backend deliberately
routes around. No FlagGems liboperators exists for the XPU SDK, so the
C++ wrappers stay off.

FLAGOS_BUILD_VENDOR.reason: xdnn_pytorch is the only operator library the XPU SDK provides

FLAGOS_BUILD_FLAGGEMS_CPP.reason: no FlagGems liboperators.so exists for the XPU SDK

_comment: Iluvatar BI-V150 (Tianshu), corex 4.5.0 SDK. The SDK is CUDA-shaped
(cuda_runtime.h, libcudart.so.10.2, libcupti.so.10.2) and the vendor
torch is a real CUDA build exporting c10::cuda, so the runtime sources
are the shared cuda/ ones and c10/cuda headers compile. But this is NOT
a boxing platform: there is no FlagGems liboperators.so for corex, and
ops route to the FlagGems Python path (FlagTree Triton, iluvatar
backend) through backends_iluvatar.conf. Boxing stays off, so the CUDA
boxing kernels and the flaggems_cpp/tileops modes are all disabled.
The wheel carries a local version segment (corex4.5.0) but no pypi_lane:
there is no self-hosted iluvatar CI runner yet, so the platform builds
and installs locally without being published.

FLAGOS_BUILD_FLAGGEMS_CPP.reason: no FlagGems liboperators.so exists for corex

FLAGOS_BUILD_BOXING.reason: FlagGems-primary: ops route to the FlagTree Triton iluvatar backend, not the CUDA boxing kernels

_comment: Huawei CANN: ACLNN is the only operator library, FlagGems Python is on by
default (FlagTree Triton), boxing is off (the conf routes nothing to the
CUDA boxing kernels).

FLAGOS_BUILD_VENDOR.reason: ACLNN is the only operator library the CANN toolkit provides

_comment: TsingMicro Kuiper: no vendor backend directory exists, so FLAGOS_BUILD_VENDOR
is a no-op. FlagGems Python is the operator path; boxing is an explicit opt-in,
so the default wheel compiles no CUDA boxing kernels. Nothing routes to them
anyway -- backends_tsingmicro.conf names no `cuda` entry -- but the switch no
longer compiles kernels the conf never selects.
FlagGems C++ is OFF, unlike cuda: it links liboperators.so, and no FlagGems
wheel carries one (flag_gems ships py3-none-any). CMakeLists.txt makes a
missing FlagGems_DIR a FATAL_ERROR, so leaving it on turns `pip install` for
this platform into a configure failure unless the user has built FlagGems
from source. Nothing routes to flaggems_cpp here either. Same as dcu/musa/bpu.
Hygon DTK: the vendor torch is a hipified build registering its HIP
kernels under the CUDA key, so the generated boxing kernels dispatch into
libtorch_hip.so unchanged. No FlagGems liboperators exists for DTK.
FlagGems-primary by default: FLAGOS_BUILD_BOXING is off, so the default
wheel needs no vendor torch package and routes to FlagGems (cpu_fallback
for the rest). A boxing wheel is an explicit opt-in.

FLAGOS_BUILD_FLAGGEMS_CPP.reason: no FlagGems liboperators.so exists for DTK

_comment: Enflame GCU: no CUDA runtime, topsaten provides the native compute ops
(FLAGOS_BUILD_VENDOR), ops without a topsaten kernel fall back to CPU.
FlagGems Python shares the same dispatcher; boxing is off.
Moore Threads MUSA: native operator route (mudnn), no CUDA runtime, so
boxing is off and the vendor kernels are mandatory. FlagGems Python is on
for the hybrid path.

FLAGOS_BUILD_VENDOR.reason: mudnn is the only kernel source this toolchain can build

FLAGOS_BUILD_FLAGGEMS_CPP.reason: no FlagGems liboperators.so exists for MUSA

_comment: D-Robotics RDK BPU: no per-op kernels, only the runtime layer (UCP
allocator, device/stream stubs) is native. FLAGOS_BUILD_VENDOR stays at the
ON default but compiles nothing (backends/bpu/ does not exist).
FLAGOS_BUILD_BOXING is off: backends_bpu.conf names no `cuda` entry and the
platform registers no compute ops at all, so the boxing kernels were
compiled but never reachable. Acceleration is the torch.compile backend.

FLAGOS_BUILD_FLAGGEMS_CPP.reason: the BPU executes compiled graphs and has no per-operator kernels at all

_comment: Apple Silicon (M-series) via Metal. A native backend, not a boxing one:
no CUDA runtime exists and none is faked, so boxing, FlagGems and FlagTree
are all off (there is no Metal Triton line to build against).
csrc/runtime/accelerator/mps/ is Objective-C++ (OBJCXX) because Metal is an
Objective-C API; the runtime links -framework Metal/-framework Foundation.
FLAGOS_BUILD_VENDOR is ON so the stage-1 operator tree (backends/mps/, an
MPSGraph-first wrapper set) compiles once it exists; with no such directory
yet it is a no-op, exactly as for bpu.

FLAGOS_BUILD_FLAGGEMS_CPP.reason: no FlagGems liboperators.so exists for the Metal stack
